ai.description: *Micrixalus sali* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored belly. It features a distinct white throat patch and males perform rhythmic foot-flagging displays near streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus sali* is best distinguished by its distinctively bright, lime-green dorsal coloration, which contrasts sharply with the duller, mottled patterns of other dancing frogs.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus sali* inhabits the shaded, rocky stream beds of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, male *Micrixalus sali* perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, extending and waving their hind legs to attract mates and signal rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus sali* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in hidden nests beneath stream-bed gravel and boulders.
ai.distributionRemarks: Micrixalus sali is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting the evergreen forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Micrixalus sali* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted by males while perched on rocks along fast-flowing streams.
